# 1494 Labs

# Fund, partnership and portfolio accounting for fund managers, allocators and fund administrators.

## [Who it is for](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- Managers (GPs): hedge funds, private equity, credit and real estate funds, registered funds, RICs and BDCs. Fund and investor accounting, fees, waterfalls and carry, investor statements and regulatory filings.

- Allocators (LPs): fund of funds, family offices, endowments, foundations and other institutional investors. Commitments, calls and distributions across every underlying fund, look-through to the holdings, and performance by vintage, strategy and manager.

- Administrators: many funds with different terms on one platform, and reconciliation against bank, custodian and administrator files.

- [Fund, Partnership and Investor Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- [Hedge Fund Accounting](https://1494labs.com/hedge-fund-accounting/)

- [Private Equity Fund Accounting](https://1494labs.com/private-equity-fund-accounting/)

- [Registered Fund Accounting](https://1494labs.com/registered-fund-accounting/)

- [Family Office Accounting](https://1494labs.com/family-office-accounting/)

- [Fund Administration Software](https://1494labs.com/fund-administration-software/)

- [Fund of Funds Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

- [Endowment and Foundation Investment Accounting](https://1494labs.com/endowment-and-foundation-investment-accounting/)

## [Partnership and investor accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- Subscriptions, redemptions, transfers, calls, commitments, distributions and recallable capital.

- Equalization or series accounting, chosen per fund. High-water marks carried per investor through partial redemptions, transfers and restatements.

- Management and incentive fees, offsets, waterfalls with carry, clawback and vesting, and side pockets.

- Allocations by class, series and sleeve, and investor NAV in the class currency.

## [Complex structures](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

- Master-feeder, alternative investment vehicles (AIVs), SPVs, blockers, co-investments and continuation vehicles.

- Holding companies, family partnerships, trusts and GRATs, SMAs and funds of one, and personal accounts, with ownership traced through every layer.

- Blocker tax accrued at the entity and carried to each investor behind it.

- Fund of funds look-through to the underlying holdings, on both ownership bases.

## [Portfolio accounting across asset classes](https://1494labs.com/portfolio-accounting/)

- Public and private equity, fixed income, loans, credit facilities on both sides, real estate and REITs, derivatives, hedge fund and private fund interests, and digital assets, in any currency.

## [Portfolio companies](https://1494labs.com/portfolio-company-kpi-collection/)

- Financials and KPIs collected from each company by upload or a secure submission link: revenue, EBITDA, net debt and the metrics you define, checked on the way in.

- Every submission and correction kept with its reporting date, currency, source and submitter.

- Collected figures shown beside each valuation mark, and the submission used recorded with it.

- Cap tables with financing rounds, tenders, vesting and exit waterfalls.

- Company financials and KPIs in fund reporting, with missing companies flagged.

## [Secondaries](https://1494labs.com/secondaries-and-strip-sale-accounting/)

- Buy and sell LP interests, single or as a strip sale across many funds in one transaction.

- Purchase-price adjustments and deferred payments at a discount, with interim flows between the reference date and closing.

- The day-one gain between price paid and fair value recognized at acquisition, and cost basis kept.

- GP-led deals: continuation vehicles and tender offers.

- Direct secondaries in common stock, valued with waterfall and option-pricing methods.

- A secondaries portfolio report, and buyer and seller confirmations.

## [Liquidity and forecasting](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

- Cash projection in horizon buckets out past a year, from settled cash: expected proceeds from underlying funds, investor outflows, unfunded commitments and scheduled obligations.

- Available liquidity including undrawn credit facilities.

- Commitment pacing for fund of funds and allocator programs.

- Deployment and exit forecasts for drawdown funds, with fees and fund-level debt.

- Cash-flow plans for evergreen, real estate and credit books: dealing, property recoveries, loan draws, interest and repayments.

- Scenarios with frozen inputs, each projected amount traced to the records behind it, and past forecasts kept.

- Gates, lockups and notice periods tracked for every underlying fund.

## [Close, controls and reconciliation](https://1494labs.com/close-controls-and-reconciliation/)

- Period close with a frozen trial balance and graded revisions.

- Official and latest-knowledge books on one ledger, with the source of every line.

- Cash, positions and NAV reconciled against outside files, with an exceptions worklist.

- A check that recomputes every fund's arithmetic each morning.

## [Reporting](https://1494labs.com/fund-and-investor-reporting/)

- NAV, capital account statements, ILPA notices, performance, and Form PF and Form ADV answers from the same book.

- Saved analyses that refresh on the platform and can be pulled through the API.

## [API and AI](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-api-and-ai/)

- Everything on screen is also in the public API.

- AI assistants read the book through MCP.

- AI reads statements and LPAs, and a person confirms each result before it posts.

The capability matrix lists product scope and status.

## Demo, sandbox and assistant access

- [Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact): describe your fund and current workflow, or email hello@1494labs.com. Ask for a sandbox seeded with reference funds.
- [Capabilities](https://1494labs.com/capabilities.md): current product scope and status.
- [Connect an assistant](https://1494labs.com/connect-assistant.md): endpoint, authentication, tools and a synthetic example.
- MCP: POST /api/v1/mcp on your workspace's application origin. Requires ordinary workspace authentication and respects the user's permissions. Tools read the book and run saved analyses; this is not an anonymous public demo endpoint. Ask hello@1494labs.com about connecting your assistant.

# Blocker Corporation Accounting

For fund managers, allocators and administrators accounting for investors through blockers.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Master-feeder, alternative investment vehicles (AIVs), SPVs, blockers, co-investments and continuation vehicles.

- Blocker tax accrued at the entity and carried to each investor behind it.

## Related Notes

- [What an opening balance has to carry](https://1494labs.com/notes/what-an-opening-balance-has-to-carry/)

- [ABOR and IBOR](https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/)

- [Fund Accounting Glossary](https://1494labs.com/glossary/)

- [Capabilities and Status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

## Questions

### Does 1494 Labs handle blocker corporations?

Accrue tax in the blocker corporation and carry each investor's share through the structure.

# Fund Accounting Capabilities

39 capabilities for fund managers, allocators and fund administrators, with current status and accounting scope.

## Partnership and Investor Accounting

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [Equalization](https://1494labs.com/notes/equalization-and-the-mid-period-subscriber/) or series accounting, chosen per fund | Shipped |
| Both the equalization-factor and series approaches, per fund. | |
| [High-water marks](https://1494labs.com/notes/high-water-marks-and-partial-redemptions/) carried per investor | Shipped |
| The mark survives partial redemption, transfer and restatement | Shipped |
| Side pockets that split dealing NAV from total NAV | Shipped |
| Configurable [waterfall tiers](https://1494labs.com/notes/european-vs-american-waterfall/) | Shipped |
| Carry accrual, clawback and per-principal vesting | Shipped |
| Class-currency investor NAV | Shipped |
| Fund-of-funds look-through, on both ownership bases | Shipped |
| Share of the underlying fund needs a manager-reported size and is absent with a stated reason when they do not report one. | |
| Multi-level family-office ownership | Shipped |

## The ledger

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Official and latest-knowledge books on one ledger, with the source of every line | Shipped |
| Each line can show how it would read under the other book, and the difference is exact because both figures come from the ledger itself. | |
| Multi-asset on one book | Shipped |
| Drawdown commitments, calls and distributions | Shipped |
| ILPA call/distribution notices and line-item codes | Shipped |
| RIC and BDC operations | Shipped |
| Multi-currency billing with the rate stamped at both ends | Shipped |
| Frozen trial balance at close, with graded revisions | Shipped |
| Credit facilities on both sides: the fund's own borrowing lines and the loans it makes | Shipped |
| Subscription lines and asset-based lines carry a borrowing base, draws, repayments and interest. Loans the fund makes carry their terms, servicing events and cash receipts. | |
| Form PF and Form ADV Schedule D answers derived from the book | Shipped |
| Each answer cites the rows it came from, and a missing input shows as an explicit gap. Exported for a compliance vendor or prepared for filing. | |
| Form PF inputs the ledger does not hold, entered on review screens and signed | Shipped |
| Portfolio-company financials, valuation procedures, beneficial owners and related persons are entered on review screens, drafted from the book where it has the answer, and signed. A correction adds a new signature and keeps the earlier one. Beneficial owners come from the investor's KYC record. | |

## Structures, Portfolio Companies and Forecasting

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Blocker tax accrued at the entity and carried to each investor behind it | In progress |
| Secondaries and strip sale accounting | Shipped |
| Portfolio-company financials and KPI collection | Shipped |
| Liquidity projection and available undrawn credit | Shipped |
| Commitment pacing and cash-flow forecasts | Shipped |

## How you get at it

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| An LP-facing investor portal | Shipped |
| Investors sign in to view and download documents made available to them. | |
| Everything you can do on screen, available through the public API | Shipped |
| Saved analyses that refresh on the platform and can be pulled by other systems through the API | Shipped |
| [AI assistants can read the book through MCP](https://1494labs.com/connect-assistant/), the standard connector for AI tools | Shipped |
| AI extraction from statements and LPAs, with mandatory human confirmation | Shipped |
| Nothing AI-derived posts without a person confirming it. | |
| A daily check that recomputes the arithmetic on every fund on the platform | Shipped |
| Capital accounts against the ledger, allocations against the pool, cash movements against the entries that produced them. | |
| Internal exceptions: a worklist, aging, and an accept-with-a-note decision | Shipped |
| An exception names the fund, the period and the amount. The check proves the book agrees with itself. Whether a price was right is a separate question, answered by checking against a custodian's numbers. | |
| External exceptions: cash against an imported bank statement, positions against a custodian's file | Shipped |
| A statement's lines auto-match the book only when exactly one movement fits; anything else is left for a person, and what is left over raises an exception on the same worklist as the internal ones. | |
| External exceptions: NAV against an outside administrator's file | Shipped |
| The Shadow tab ties an administrator's pack (fund and class NAV, capital accounts, trial balance, cash, positions, fees) to the book from CSV or XLSX, remembers each administrator's column layout, and raises every difference on the same exceptions worklist. | |

## What we do not do

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Order and execution management | No |
| We are the book of record. There is no order ticket and there will not be one. | |
| Custody, or moving money | No |
| The platform produces the payment file an operator carries to their banking portal. It holds no credentials for any bank or payment system and initiates no transfers. | |
| Tax return preparation and K-1 filing | No |
| Private per-fund book-data preparer workpapers are available under reporting (#1702), with unresolved character and tax-input gaps. Final tax allocations, tax-basis capital, withholding and K-1 preparation/filing remain with the preparer. Owner/preparer review is required before a demonstration claim. | |
| Market data and pricing feeds we supply | No |
| Bring your own provider. We provide the connection that loads your provider's feed and will not resell data or imply a license we do not hold. | |
| A third-party security attestation | Roadmap 2027Q2 |
| No report today. The security page lists the controls that are in place and the ones that are not. | |
| A native mobile application | No |
| The web app renders and is navigable at phone width. There is no native app and none is planned. | |

# Capital Call and Distribution Software

For fund managers, allocators and administrators tracking investor commitments and cash flows.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Subscriptions, redemptions, transfers, calls, commitments, distributions and recallable capital.

- NAV, capital account statements, ILPA notices, performance, and Form PF and Form ADV answers from the same book.

- Commitment pacing for fund of funds and allocator programs.

## Related Notes

- [Capabilities and Status](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/)

## Questions

### Can I track recallable capital alongside calls and distributions?

Keep recallable capital with the investor's commitments, calls and distribution records, and prepare ILPA notices from the book.

# 1494 Labs vs Allvue Fund Accounting

A fund accounting comparison for a private equity team closing the ledger and investor capital accounts together. Use a worked close to test the fit.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

Allvue describes cloud fund accounting for private equity and fund administrators, with a multi-currency general ledger, partnership accounting and financial reporting. Source: [Allvue Fund Accounting product page](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

## What to compare in a demonstration

| Workflow | Allvue Fund Accounting: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | It describes a multi-currency general ledger and partnership accounting. [Source](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Fees and allocations | Its optional waterfall module models LPA terms and carry calculations. [Source](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes a financial report library, a flexible report writer and standardized workflows. [Source](https://www.allvuesystems.com/solutions/fund-accounting/) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Prove a private equity close from source to statement

Choose one fund with contributions, expenses and an investment exit. Configure its agreement terms, calculate the allocation and distribution, and trace the investor statement to the ledger. Include a correction in the open period and confirm that the calculation and its entries can be reviewed again.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

[Request a 1494 Labs demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact) with your fund structure and one close you want to reproduce. You can also read [1494 Labs as an alternative to Allvue](https://1494labs.com/compare/allvue-alternative/) or [browse the comparison guides](https://1494labs.com/compare/).

# 1494 Labs vs FIS Private Capital Suite

A fund accounting comparison for a private capital team evaluating fund accounting, carry and investor reporting. Use a worked close to test the fit.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

FIS Private Capital Suite, formerly Investran, is described by FIS as a platform for fund and partnership accounting and automated investor reporting. Source: [FIS Private Capital Suite product page](https://www.fisglobal.com/products/fis-private-capital-suite), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

## What to compare in a demonstration

| Workflow | FIS Private Capital Suite: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | FIS describes automation of fund and partnership accounting. [Source](https://www.fisglobal.com/products/fis-private-capital-suite) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Fees and allocations | Its product material describes digital waterfall administration and automated carry calculations. [Source](https://www.fisglobal.com/products/fis-private-capital-suite) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes automated investor reporting and access to portfolio and performance data. [Source](https://www.fisglobal.com/products/fis-private-capital-suite) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Compare waterfall results under the fund's agreement

Bring two exits with different dates and a later capital call. Specify whether the waterfall is whole-of-fund or deal-by-deal, and agree the preferred-return and catch-up terms. Follow the LP and GP amounts through the calculation and ledger. Add a dated correction and explain the change in the result.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

[Request a 1494 Labs demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact) with your fund structure and one close you want to reproduce. You can also read [1494 Labs as an alternative to FIS Private Capital Suite / Investran](https://1494labs.com/compare/fis-investran-alternative/) or [browse the comparison guides](https://1494labs.com/compare/).

# 1494 Labs vs FundCount

A fund accounting comparison for a family office or fund team keeping investment and investor records together. Use a worked close to test the fit.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

FundCount describes partnership and portfolio accounting posted to the same general ledger, including capital accounts, allocations and waterfalls. Source: [FundCount partnership accounting](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

## What to compare in a demonstration

| Workflow | FundCount: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | Capital activity and partner allocations post to its general ledger. [Source](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Fees and allocations | Its partnership page describes configurable preferred returns, catch-up and carry splits. [Source](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes on-demand capital statements and partner-level rollforwards. [Source](https://fundcount.com/solutions/partnership-accounting/) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Work through a multi-entity capital movement

Use a parent entity, an investment vehicle and two participating investors. Post an investment valuation, an expense and a distribution. Follow each investor's share through the ownership structure, then reconcile the entity balances and consolidated view. Change one source amount and review the resulting allocations and entries.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

LemonEdge describes fund accounting for complex private equity structures, with event-based partnership accounting and allocation paths for ownership, carry and waterfalls. Source: [LemonEdge private equity product page](https://www.lemonedge.com/markets/private-equity), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

| Workflow | LemonEdge: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | It describes event-based partnership accounting for multi-entity structures. [Source](https://www.lemonedge.com/markets/private-equity) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Fees and allocations | Its allocation paths cover ownership, carry and waterfalls. [Source](https://www.lemonedge.com/markets/private-equity) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes auditable, time-stamped calculations against live data. [Source](https://www.lemonedge.com/markets/private-equity) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Follow an allocation through the ownership structure

Model the actual ownership chain with a feeder and underlying vehicle. Post income and an expense in the underlying book, then follow their allocation to the feeder's investors. Inspect the ownership basis, currency treatment and ledger entries. Reconcile the combined view to the individual books.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

# 1494 Labs vs SS&C Geneva

A fund accounting comparison for a hedge fund team reviewing its investment book and investor accounting. Use a worked close to test the fit.

Product sources reviewed November 3, 2026

## Start with the accounting workflow

SS&C Advent describes Geneva as a platform for portfolio and fund management, investor accounting and reporting, and shadow accounting. Source: [SS&C Advent Geneva product page](https://www.advent.com/geneva/), reviewed November 3, 2026.

1494 Labs configures fees, allocations and waterfalls to the fund's agreement. Investment records and investor capital accounts meet in one ledger, with recurring checks and a trail from a reported balance to its entries. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

## What to compare in a demonstration

| Workflow | SS&C Geneva: published description | 1494 Labs: demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The accounting record | It describes portfolio and fund management with multi-currency accounting. [Source](https://www.advent.com/geneva/) | 1494 Labs keeps investment and investor accounting on one ledger. Trace a capital account to its allocations and entries. |
| Investor accounting | Its product page includes investor accounting and reporting. [Source](https://www.advent.com/geneva/) | Configure fees and waterfalls to the fund's agreement, then inspect the calculation and the entries it produces. |
| Reviewing the result | It describes shadow accounting, reconciliation and exception-management workflows. [Source](https://www.advent.com/geneva/) | Trace reported balances to the book and review the recurring checks that raise exceptions when the records stop tying. |

## Reconcile the investment book and investor result

Use a representative period with a trade, a valuation change, income and an investor capital movement. Reconcile positions and cash to the ledger, then follow income and expenses into the investor allocation. Compare the book with an independent administrator statement and investigate one deliberate difference.

1. Agree the opening book, governing terms and expected results before the demonstration.

2. Run the same dated transactions and valuations in each evaluation.

3. Compare fees, investor allocations and closing balances, with an explanation for every difference.

4. Ask to follow a reported amount back through its calculation and ledger entries.

Take the expected results away with the calculation evidence. The review should show whether the proposed setup handles your fund's terms and whether your team can explain the close.

Source: https://1494labs.com/connect-assistant/

# Connect an assistant to your fund accounting workspace

Ask about funds and saved analyses through MCP, the standard connector for AI tools. Reads use your workspace permissions.

Connection guide · November 3, 2026

## What you need

An existing 1494 Labs workspace, an administrator who has enabled AI for that workspace, and an MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP with a custom Authorization header. This connection reads workspace data. There is no anonymous demo endpoint.

1. **Enable workspace AI.** An administrator enables AI under Administration › Workspace › AI & budget. When AI is off, MCP returns HTTP 403 with `ai_disabled`.

2. **Create a read-only key.** Under Administration › People & access › API Keys, choose Read-only or the specific read permissions you need. The key remains bound to its workspace and its creator's permissions. Copy the secret when shown and keep it in your client's credential store.

3. **Set the connection URL.** Use your workspace's application origin followed by `/api/v1/mcp`. For example, if you sign in at `https://your-workspace.example.com`, the URL is `https://your-workspace.example.com/api/v1/mcp`. Replace this illustrative origin with your actual workspace address; the marketing site is not the endpoint.

4. **Configure authentication.** Set `Authorization: Bearer <your-workspace-api-key>`. Use the Bearer header for this connection so credentials reach downstream reads. The endpoint also accepts a live session access token. Browser sessions use their access cookie and require the matching `X-CSRF-Token` on POST requests.

5. **Connect and discover tools.** Your client initializes the connection and lists tools. Start with `list_funds`, then discover the reads or saved analyses needed for your question.

Use a client that lets you supply the header. This endpoint does not provide an OAuth sign-in flow. If your assistant only offers OAuth connections, ask [hello@1494labs.com](mailto:hello@1494labs.com) about a compatible setup. Share credentials only through the client's credential settings, never in a conversation.

## The five tools

| Tool | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `list_funds` | Find funds by code or name and resolve their UUIDs. Optional `q` filters the list; `limit` controls the page size. |
| `search_api` | Find GET endpoints by a phrase such as "trial balance" or "capital account." Returns paths and parameters for a subsequent read. |
| `read_api` | Read a discovered `/api/v1/` path, passing its filters in `query`. Substitute real IDs for path placeholders and follow the endpoint's pagination when needed. |
| `list_saved_calcs` | Find saved analyses. Call without arguments for available grid keys, then pass a `grid_key` to list analyses on that table. Another user's private analyses are excluded. |
| `run_saved_calc` | Recompute an accessible saved analysis from the live book using its `calc_id`. Optional `fund_id`, `period_id` and `as_of` override its saved context. An empty subtotal with a reason is not zero. |

## A first question and answer

**Question:** "Which fund matches DEMO-PE? Tell me its legal name and currency."

The assistant calls `list_funds` with `{"q":"DEMO-PE","limit":10}`. Suppose the returned fund has `fund_code` DEMO-PE, `legal_name` Example Private Equity Fund LP and `base_currency_code` USD.

**Illustrative answer:** "DEMO-PE is Example Private Equity Fund LP. Its base currency is USD. Source: the workspace fund record returned by list_funds." These synthetic names and values illustrate the response. If several funds match, the assistant should ask which one you mean.

For an accounting question, keep that fund's returned `id`, use `search_api` to find the relevant read, then call `read_api` with the fund ID and the endpoint's required period parameters. Ask the assistant to name the fund, period and source, and to say when data is missing.

## Check the connection directly

A compatible client sends JSON-RPC 2.0 messages by HTTP POST with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. For example, after setting the URL and Bearer header in its connection settings, it sends:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"workspace-reader","version":"1.0"}}}
```

Read the negotiated protocol version in the response, send `notifications/initialized` without an ID, then `tools/list`:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}
```

The initialized notification returns HTTP 202 with no body. Calls return JSON. The server keeps no MCP session and has no server-push stream; a GET to the connection URL returns HTTP 405. Opening the URL in a browser is not a connection test.

## Access and troubleshooting

- **HTTP 401:** check the key or session token, its expiry and revocation state, and the workspace origin.

- **HTTP 403:** check the workspace AI setting and the permissions needed by the requested read. Seeing a tool name does not grant access to its data.

- **A tool reports an error:** check the returned reason, fund and period IDs, and the endpoint parameters. Do not turn a failed or truncated read into a financial answer.

These tools read data and compute saved results. They cannot create journals, post allocations or change fund terms. Revoking or rotating the key ends its use under the workspace's normal key policy. Choose an assistant approved by your organization for the data you intend to read.

[Request a demo or sandbox](https://1494labs.com/#contact) to try this on reference funds. See the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) for current product scope.

# Endowment and Foundation Investment Accounting

For endowment and foundation investment teams and their administrators.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Allocators (LPs): fund of funds, family offices, endowments, foundations and other institutional investors. Commitments, calls and distributions across every underlying fund, look-through to the holdings, and performance by vintage, strategy and manager.

- Fund of funds look-through to the underlying holdings, on both ownership bases.

- Cash projection in horizon buckets out past a year, from settled cash: expected proceeds from underlying funds, investor outflows, unfunded commitments and scheduled obligations.

- Available liquidity including undrawn credit facilities.

- Commitment pacing for fund of funds and allocator programs.

- NAV, capital account statements, ILPA notices, performance, and Form PF and Form ADV answers from the same book.

- Saved analyses that refresh on the platform and can be pulled through the API.

### Can I trace ownership through trusts and holding companies?

Follow ownership through holding companies, partnerships, trusts and GRATs to the investments beneath them.

## Product Screens

![An ownership structure drawn as a flow diagram: four family trusts converging on a holding company of $3.58bn, through a family partnership, out to six asset sleeves and a co-investment vehicle.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/structure-flow.49a61406.jpg)

**Four trusts, one holding company, six sleeves.** Band width is the value passing *through* each vehicle, so a holding company worth $157.5m in its legal books and controlling $3.58bn shows both values.

![The whole ownership structure as an org chart: four trusts, a holding company, a family partnership, six asset vehicles and a co-investment vehicle.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/structure-graph.60cc35a2.jpg)

**Every vehicle once, with its owners converging on it.** One vehicle can have several owners, so drawing the structure as separate trees would repeat the shared vehicles once per branch.

![A look-through consolidation showing legal books of $12.01bn against a consolidated $1.50bn, with a per-asset table giving legal owner, asset class, valuation basis, effective ownership, gross value and attributed value.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/look-through-consolidation.a6726248.jpg)

**$12.01bn of legal books, $1.50bn of it actually owned.**
The gap is the same dollar counted at each layer it passes through. Every
row carries the effective ownership that got it there (40% of $157.5m is $63.0m), computed from the capital accounts, so the
consolidation and the ownership diagram cannot disagree.

## Product Screens

![The fund overview on Home: the NAV calculated for the selected period, that period's fees, and position value and operating cash read live, with the floor the cash is measured against.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/fund-dashboard.8d533a4c.jpg)

**Each figure says which point in time it reflects.** NAV is the one calculated for the period you selected, fees are that period's, and anything read from the books as they stand now is marked Live, including the cash the fund can spend and the floor it is measured against.

![An income statement with trading gains, administration fee expense and directors' fees, totaling net income.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/income-statement.7581fcbf.jpg)

**Real operating expenses carrying their GL codes.** Expenses post through the income and expense ledger, which is also the only source the allocation to investors reads, so a cost that reaches NAV reaches capital accounts too.

![A per-investor allocation for the period: six investors by name, each with opening capital, net profit and loss, and ending capital.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/allocation-per-investor.c3091f57.jpg)

**The period's profit and loss, split across investors.** Opening $23,499,503.07, net $125,969.93, ending $23,625,473.00 - which is the NAV on the dashboard above. Fees and expenses are attributed per investor, directly to the accounts that bear them.

![A NAV restatement history listing every change to a fund's NAV with prior value, new value and delta.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/nav-restatement.f2e59da4.jpg)

**Every change to a calculated NAV keeps its own record.** The ledger keeps the trail itself, so nobody has to remember to.

![A trial balance of thirteen accounts by code and category, with debits and credits each totaling $28,515,992.43 and a cent of rounding shown on a separate line.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/trial-balance.164f78ab.jpg)

**And the ledger those statements read.** Debits and credits foot to the same $28,515,992.43, and the cent of rounding sits on a line of its own. Close the period and the trial balance is locked as a revision the system will not let anyone edit, which is what a statement produced a year later reads from.

# 1494 Labs and an outsourced fund administrator

Compare the accounting system with the service relationship, and decide which book and reconciliation your team needs to own.

Updated November 3, 2026

## Separate the service decision from the book

A fund administrator provides people and contracted services. Fund accounting software provides the system in which a team keeps and reviews the book. Scope the work first: who books transactions, calculates NAV, reviews allocations, produces investor reports and approves the close?

1494 Labs is fund accounting software for fund teams and administrators. A software demonstration should prove the accounting workflow; a service evaluation should establish responsibility, staffing, reporting deadlines and review arrangements.

## Three workflows to evaluate

- **An internal book.** Your team runs the ledger and close. Confirm that you have the people and review process for the work you retain.

- **A shadow book.** Your team maintains an independent record and compares it with the administrator's reports. Agree the data exchange, timing and break resolution.

- **An administrator-operated book.** Ask what access, exports and supporting records your team receives, and who approves adjustments.

## Test the handoff with one period

1. List the inputs each party supplies and their delivery dates.

2. Reconcile investment positions, cash and opening investor capital.

3. Compare the fee and allocation calculations under the same agreement terms.

4. Record each difference with its source, owner and resolution.

5. Agree which reports are approved and how corrections reach both teams.

1494 Labs includes shadow reconciliation for comparing an outside administrator's book with your own. Ask to see a break identified and traced to its source. For an administrator evaluating the platform, ask to see the workflow across several client funds.

Bring the proposed division of responsibilities to a [demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact). Review [fund administration workflows](https://1494labs.com/fund-administration-software/) and the [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) before agreeing the scope.


---

Source: https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software-vs-spreadsheets/

# 1494 Labs vs spreadsheets for fund accounting

Compare a spreadsheet-based fund close with a ledger that traces fees, allocations and investor balances to their entries.

Updated November 3, 2026

## Compare the work of closing a period

A useful evaluation starts with one completed period from a fund like yours. Reproduce the fee, allocation and investor statement, then change one input and follow its effect through the book.

| Controller's task | Spreadsheet workflow to inspect | 1494 Labs demonstration to request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Update a fund's fee terms | Locate the formulas and copies that depend on the term | Show the configured fee terms and the resulting calculation |
| Explain an investor balance | Trace workbook references to ledger exports | Trace the capital account to allocations and entries |
| Check the close | Review reconciliations and exception tabs | Show the checks and investigate an exception |
| Prepare the next period | Verify copied formulas, opening balances and fee state | Show the next period's opening state and calculation trail |

## Use a worked acceptance test

1. Agree the opening ledger, investor balances and fee state.

2. Run the period with the same dated transactions and terms.

3. Reconcile NAV, fees and every investor's closing balance.

4. Introduce a corrected input and inspect the affected entries and reports.

5. Save the evidence and agree who owns the accepted book.

The objective is a reproducible close. Keep independent spreadsheet checks where they help a reviewer, and make the accounting record and approval process clear.

1494 Labs supports configured fees, allocations and waterfalls with a traceable ledger and recurring checks. The [capability matrix](https://1494labs.com/capabilities/) identifies current scope and planned work. [Read the conversion checklist](https://1494labs.com/notes/moving-a-fund-off-spreadsheets/), then [request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact) using reference funds shaped like your own.

# Fund Administration Software

For fund administrators accounting for many funds with different terms.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Administrators: many funds with different terms on one platform, and reconciliation against bank, custodian and administrator files.

- Subscriptions, redemptions, transfers, calls, commitments, distributions and recallable capital.

- Equalization or series accounting, chosen per fund. High-water marks carried per investor through partial redemptions, transfers and restatements.

- Management and incentive fees, offsets, waterfalls with carry, clawback and vesting, and side pockets.

- Allocations by class, series and sleeve, and investor NAV in the class currency.

- Period close with a frozen trial balance and graded revisions.

- Official and latest-knowledge books on one ledger, with the source of every line.

- Cash, positions and NAV reconciled against outside files, with an exceptions worklist.

- A check that recomputes every fund's arithmetic each morning.

- NAV, capital account statements, ILPA notices, performance, and Form PF and Form ADV answers from the same book.

- Saved analyses that refresh on the platform and can be pulled through the API.

Each fund carries its terms for investor accounting, fees and waterfalls. Administrators can reconcile the books against bank, custodian and administrator files.

## Product Screens

![A Statement of Changes in Partners' Capital, from beginning capital through contributions, net income and fees to ending capital.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/statement-of-changes.39e06e66.jpg)

**Ending capital ties to the dashboard NAV to the cent.** Both figures come from the same ledger, so no reconciliation runs between them.

![A fee gross-to-net statement: five management fee accruals, each from gross accrual to net fee, totaling $65,934.06 gross and net with no offsets, waivers or rebates.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/fee-gross-to-net.a19c17c9.jpg)

**Gross to net, per accrual, per client.** Each posted fee keeps the steps it was calculated with, in order (gross, then offsets, waivers and rebates, then net), saved when it posted, so a later change to the terms does not rewrite it.

![An exception detail panel for the operating cash account at 2026-06-30: the bank statement's closing balance of $747,850.00 against the book's $750,000.00, a difference of $2,150.00, a reason field, and buttons to acknowledge, resolve or accept the difference.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/break-detail.dc783d42.jpg)

**Expected, actual, difference, and a decision with a name on it.**
Resolve and accept are deliberately different: resolved means the
numbers now agree, accepted means they still differ and somebody decided
that is correct. Accepting requires a note, because "they differ and
that is fine" is only institutional memory if it says why.

![A cash movements blotter of settled movements: investments into underlying managers, investor subscriptions, and transfers between the fund's own cash accounts, each with its source and counterparty.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/cash-movements.61bcbb09.jpg)

**Cash movements, with their sources.** Select many rows and act on them together in every table, because an administrator's day is spent on many rows at once.

![The exceptions worklist: two open exceptions on the operating cash account, raised by an imported bank statement. The closing balance differs from the book by $2,150.00, and one statement line of -$2,150.00 matches nothing in the book.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/reconciliation-breaks.3b91eb16.jpg)

**A finding has somewhere to go.**
An imported bank statement matched every line but one, a $2,150 fee
the book never recorded, and raised two exceptions: the balance and the unmatched line. An exception ages, gets assigned, and keeps what was decided
about it, so next month's exception on the same account arrives with
last month's reasoning attached.

# Fund of Funds Accounting

For fund of funds managers, allocators and their administrators.

## Accounting Capabilities

- Allocators (LPs): fund of funds, family offices, endowments, foundations and other institutional investors. Commitments, calls and distributions across every underlying fund, look-through to the holdings, and performance by vintage, strategy and manager.

- Fund of funds look-through to the underlying holdings, on both ownership bases.

- Cash projection in horizon buckets out past a year, from settled cash: expected proceeds from underlying funds, investor outflows, unfunded commitments and scheduled obligations.

- Available liquidity including undrawn credit facilities.

- Commitment pacing for fund of funds and allocator programs.

- Scenarios with frozen inputs, each projected amount traced to the records behind it, and past forecasts kept.

- Gates, lockups and notice periods tracked for every underlying fund.

- NAV, capital account statements, ILPA notices, performance, and Form PF and Form ADV answers from the same book.

- Saved analyses that refresh on the platform and can be pulled through the API.

# Fund Accounting Glossary

Terms for fund managers, allocators and administrators reviewing investor capital, structures and portfolio cash flows.

## Blocker

A corporation held between investors and investments, with tax accounted for at that entity.

[Blocker Corporation Accounting](https://1494labs.com/blocker-corporation-accounting/)

## AIV

An alternative investment vehicle used alongside a fund to hold an investment.

[Holding Company and Family Office Entity Accounting](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

## SPV

A special purpose vehicle formed to hold a particular investment or group of investments.

[Holding Company and Family Office Entity Accounting](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

## Holdco

A holding company that owns interests in other entities.

[Holding Company and Family Office Entity Accounting](https://1494labs.com/holding-company-and-family-office-entity-accounting/)

## Strip sale

A sale of LP interests across several underlying funds in one transaction.

[Secondaries and Strip Sale Accounting](https://1494labs.com/secondaries-and-strip-sale-accounting/)

## Continuation vehicle

A vehicle that acquires investments from an existing fund in a GP-led secondary transaction.

[Secondaries for Fund of Funds](https://1494labs.com/secondaries-for-fund-of-funds/)

## Equalization

An investor-level adjustment used to allocate incentive fees when investors subscribe at different values.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## Series accounting

Separate subscription series used to track investor entry values and fee calculations.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## High-water mark

The value an investor must recover before further performance becomes subject to an incentive fee under the agreed terms.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## Crystallization

The point when an accrued incentive fee becomes payable under the fund terms.

[Equalization and Series Accounting](https://1494labs.com/equalization-and-series-accounting/)

## Side pocket

An investment pool with participation accounted for separately from the main dealing pool.

[Side Pocket Accounting](https://1494labs.com/side-pocket-accounting/)

## Look-through

A view of the holdings behind an investment in another fund or entity.

[Fund of Funds Accounting](https://1494labs.com/fund-of-funds-accounting/)

## Recallable capital

Distributed capital that the fund may call again under its agreement.

[Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

## Unfunded commitment

The remaining amount an investor has committed and may still be called to contribute.

[Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

## Commitment pacing

Planning the timing and size of commitments to underlying funds.

[Liquidity Forecasting and Commitment Pacing](https://1494labs.com/liquidity-forecasting-and-commitment-pacing/)

## Clawback

A requirement to return excess carry under the terms of the fund agreement.

[Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting](https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/)

## Hurdle

A return threshold used in calculating carried interest or incentive fees.

[Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting](https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/)

## Catch-up

A waterfall tier that allocates proceeds to bring the carry recipient to the agreed share.

[Waterfall and Carried Interest Accounting](https://1494labs.com/waterfall-and-carried-interest-accounting/)

## ILPA notice

A capital call or distribution notice using the applicable ILPA reporting format.

[Capital Call and Distribution Software](https://1494labs.com/capital-call-and-distribution-software/)

## Follow one month from income to investor capital.

One month of a reference fund, in two steps: what the fund earned after
its management fee, then where it ended up in six investors' capital accounts.

| Net income for the month | $145,284.59 |
| --- | --- |
| Management fee, through the fee calculation | −$19,314.66 |
| Net profit and loss to allocate | $125,969.93 |

| Opening investor capital | $23,499,503.07 |
| --- | --- |
| Net profit and loss allocated | +$125,969.93 |
| Ending investor capital, and the NAV | $23,625,473.00 |

| Investor account | Opening | Net P&L | Ending |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WBE-001-A | $6,284,337.90 | $33,687.42 | $6,318,025.32 |
| WBE-003-A | $5,459,391.06 | $29,265.26 | $5,488,656.32 |
| WBE-006-A | $3,774,244.32 | $20,231.97 | $3,794,476.29 |
| WBE-002-A | $3,420,147.35 | $18,333.82 | $3,438,481.17 |
| WBE-005-A | $2,519,062.68 | $13,503.53 | $2,532,566.21 |
| WBE-004-A | $2,042,319.76 | $10,947.93 | $2,053,267.69 |
| Six accounts | $23,499,503.07 | $125,969.93 | $23,625,473.00 |

**Six investor accounts reconcile to the fund's ending NAV of $23,625,473.00.** Management fees and expenses are attributed to the accounts that bear them, so a fee that reaches NAV reaches the capital account it belongs to.

# A wrong number that agrees with itself

Cash reconciles against the custodian, positions against the administrator.
Both work by comparison, so both are quiet when a figure is wrong and
nothing else in the system holds a second copy of it to disagree.

Controls · roughly 6 minutes

## Where comparison controls stop

Most controls in fund accounting are comparisons: cash against the
custodian, positions against the administrator, the general ledger against
the sub-ledger. They find a great deal. All of them work the same way,
which is that they fire when two records of the same thing differ.

A management fee charged on the wrong base has no second record. Nor does
an allocation that split a period's profit on a stale ownership percentage,
or a high-water mark that was never reduced when an investor redeemed half
their holding. In each case the books balance, every statement foots, and
the investor's capital account is internally consistent. The money was either never charged or charged to the wrong person.

Why this class survives

An audit tests whether the books are consistent, and they are. These
errors tend to surface years later, when somebody rebuilds a fee from
first principles and finds it does not come out where it was booked.

## Doing the arithmetic a second time

A figure with no counterparty to check against has to be checked against
itself: derived again by a different route, from different inputs, and
compared. We do that to every fund on the platform each morning, before
anyone signs in.

Some of what is recomputed:

- ✓**Every capital account rolls forward.**
Opening, plus contributions and withdrawals, plus that account's share of
profit and loss, equals closing, to the penny, with no tolerance, for every account in every period.

- ✓**Ownership sums to one hundred percent**
exactly, with the rounding residual placed deliberately.

- ✓**The fees charged to investors add up to the fee the fund paid**,
side letters and differing rates included. If the parts do not sum to the
pool, one of the two figures is wrong.

- ✓**Every journal entry balances and the trial balance foots**,
checked daily.

- ✓**What a position is carried at agrees with the ledger's carrying value**
through every subscription, redemption and return of capital, so the two
cannot drift apart between valuations.

A failure opens an exception on the same worklist as a cash exception, carrying the
fund, the period, and the two figures that should have agreed.

## Every morning

An error found during the close is found under deadline, by the person with
least appetite for it, when the remaining options are poor. The same error
found on a Tuesday is an afternoon's work, which is most of the argument for running the checks daily.

They also do not sample. Every fund is recomputed every day, including the
ones with no activity, because an absence of activity is itself worth
testing: a fund that has quietly stopped receiving data looks the same as a
fund having a slow month until the quarter closes.

## Knowing whether a check actually ran

A check that never ran reports nothing. A check that ran and passed also
reports nothing. On a dashboard the two are indistinguishable, and the more
conditional a check is, the more often it is the first one.

A rule that applies only to funds with an incentive fee has nothing to
examine in a book that has none. It stays quiet, and so does a rule that ran
and found nothing wrong.

The distinction

A check that has never had anything to examine has not passed. Counting
it alongside the ones that did overstates what the system has actually
demonstrated.

So the morning run reports what was never exercised as well as what failed,
naming each check that no fund gave it anything to work on. Some of that is
expected, and it says so: a rule about converted funds has nothing to
report on a book containing none. The rest is genuinely untested, and it is listed as untested.

## Leaving a cell empty

The same rule applies in the reports. Where a figure cannot be computed honestly, the cell is empty and carries
its reason. A subtotal that would be
meaningless is omitted. A percentage that has lost its denominator does not
substitute one.

Somebody queries an empty cell. Nobody queries a number that looks
reasonable, which is how a wrong one ends up in an investor statement.

## What to ask any vendor

- ✓**Which figures are recomputed, and which are stored and read back?**
A figure computed once and read thereafter has nothing in the system able
to disagree with it.

- ✓**How often do the checks run, and across how many funds?**
At period end on a sample, or daily across all of them.

- ✓**Can you show me a check that did not run?**
If everything passes, ask how the system tells a pass from a check that
had nothing to examine.

- ✓**Where does a failure go?**
Ask whether it reaches a log or a worklist with an owner.

- [Which columns can be added, and which cannot](https://1494labs.com/notes/which-columns-can-be-added/), where the empty cell comes from

- [High-water marks and the partial redemption](https://1494labs.com/notes/high-water-marks-and-partial-redemptions/), one error of this kind, in numbers

- [What the platform does](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- [Cash and reconciliation](https://docs.1494labs.com/guide/cash-and-reconciliation/) in the product docs: how cash is matched against the ledger

## How we handle it

The checks are part of how the platform is built.
A rule is written as a statement that must hold for every fund, and it
runs against every fund from then on: daily, and again after every
release. It reports what was never exercised alongside what failed. The
most recent run before this note was published covered every fund on the
platform and came back clean.

[Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact)

Source: https://1494labs.com/notes/abor-and-ibor/

# ABOR and IBOR, and why most systems keep them apart

Two books, two clocks, and a reconciliation between them that nobody wants to
own. The split is a historical accident that hardened into an architecture, and
it is worth understanding before you buy a system that assumes it.

Fund accounting · roughly 6 minutes

## Accounting and Investment Books

The **accounting book of record** is the official set of books. It
is what the auditor examines, what the administrator calculates NAV from, and what
the financial statements are built on. It follows an accounting basis, respects
period boundaries, and is deliberately conservative about recognizing things
that have not happened yet.

The **investment book of record** is the position view the
investment team works from. It answers a different question: what do we own
right now, including the trade executed twenty minutes ago that will not settle
until Wednesday, and the corporate action that has been announced but not paid.

Both are correct. They disagree because they answer different questions on different clocks,
and that disagreement is expected. The trouble is what most firms have to
do about it.

## Why they diverge

Four sources of difference account for nearly all of it.

Where the two books part company

| Dimension | Accounting book | Investment book |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Clock** | Period-bounded, closed and locked | Continuous, intraday |
| **Recognition** | Trade date or settlement date, per policy, applied consistently | Everything known, including unsettled and pending |
| **Valuation** | Accounting basis, with a documented pricing hierarchy | Live or last marks, whatever is freshest |
| **Audience** | Auditors, administrators, LPs, regulators | Portfolio managers, risk, trading |

Say you buy a position on Monday, settling Wednesday, and the month ends
Tuesday.

The investment book shows the position on Monday, because you own the economic
exposure from the moment the trade is executed. The accounting book shows it on
Monday too if your policy is trade date, or on Wednesday if it is settlement
date, which means the position falls in the following month and the month-end
statements do not include it. Both answers are defensible under the right policy, because they answer
different questions.

## Why the split became architectural

The reason is historical, which is what makes it worth questioning.

Accounting systems were built for periodic close. They ran in batches, were designed around a monthly cycle, and optimized for producing a defensible
answer slowly. That was the right design when the alternative was paper.

Front offices needed something the accounting system could not give them: a
position view current as of this morning. So
a second system grew up beside the first, fed by the same trade files, keeping
its own version of the truth.

Once two systems hold overlapping data, a third thing appears whether anyone
designed it or not: **the reconciliation between them**. And
because that reconciliation is genuinely hard, an industry grew around it. Several
vendors now sell the reconciliation itself, which makes the split a source of
revenue for the people best placed to remove it.

The tell

If a platform sells you a reconciliation module between its own accounting
and its own position data, you are being sold a bridge between two
systems that arrived in one invoice.

## What the split actually costs

### A break list that never reaches zero

Every operations team that runs this architecture has a break list, and the
break list is never empty. Some breaks are real and matter. Most are timing
differences that will resolve themselves in two days. The expensive part is that
**a genuine problem sits in that list beside forty that will clear
themselves**, and people stop reading a list that has cried wolf for
six months.

### You cannot answer the obvious question

"What is our NAV right now?" is a reasonable question and, in a two-system
architecture, an unanswerable one. The accounting book knows as of the last
close. The investment book knows positions but not the accounting treatment.
Producing a current number means a person assembling it, which means it arrives
late and carries no assurance.

### Nobody can say which one is right

This is the corrosive one. When the two books disagree by a material amount and
the answer is needed today, someone has to adjudicate. That person is usually
the most senior operations person available, and their judgment is not
auditable. Over time the organization learns which book to trust for which
question, and that knowledge lives only in people's heads.

## The alternative, and what it actually requires

The alternative is to stop treating them as two books and start treating them
as **two views of one event stream**. Every economic event is
recorded once. Trade date and settlement date become two views of the same journal entries. The accounting view applies
period boundaries and recognition policy; the investment view does not. Neither
holds data the other lacks.

Under that design there is only one record, so there is no reconciliation
to automate. When a vendor says "our reconciliation is very good", it is
describing two books, and you should know which of the two designs you
are being shown.

It is also harder to build, for four reasons.

- **Every event must create its journal entry in one place.** The
moment any part of the system records a position without a journal entry, you have two books
again and you will not notice for a month.

- **The detail on each entry has to be rich enough for both audiences.**
Entity, fund, class, series, sleeve, currency, counterparty, custodian. If
the accounting model is thinner than the investment model, the investment
view has to be rebuilt somewhere else, and you are back where you started.

- **Close has to lock the period without stopping current work.** A
closed period must stay fixed for reporting while the current view keeps moving. Getting this
wrong in the safe direction gives you a system nobody can use intraday.

- **The agreement needs continuous proof.** If the two views are designed to agree, that agreement should still be
checked continuously, because designs fail quietly.

![A Statement of Changes in Partners' Capital, with beginning capital, contributions, allocations and ending capital.](https://1494labs.com/assets/screens/statement-of-changes.39e06e66.jpg)

**What one book looks like from the accounting side.**
This statement comes from the same journal entries the position and
exposure screens use, which is why its ending capital ties to the fund's
NAV to the cent. There is no extract between them to go stale.

## Four questions for a vendor

If you are evaluating platforms, these separate the architectures faster than a
feature matrix will.

1. **Where does the reconciliation between your accounting and position
data live?** If there is one, they are two systems. That may still be
the right purchase, but you should know what you are buying.

2. **When the two disagree, which one is authoritative, and who decides?**
A good answer names a rule. A bad answer names a person.

3. **Can you produce a NAV as of right now?**
Ask to see it done in the demo.

4. **What checks that the books are internally consistent, and how often
does it run?** "Our architecture guarantees it" is an assertion.
"These checks run every morning and here is today's output" is evidence.

A caveat worth stating

One ledger is not automatically the right answer for every firm. If your
accounting is genuinely simple and your investment process is genuinely
complex, or the reverse, two specialized systems and a small reconciliation
may cost less than migrating. The argument here is that the split should be a decision you made. Too
often it is an architecture inherited because that is how the software
was sold in 1998.

- [What an opening balance has to carry](https://1494labs.com/notes/what-an-opening-balance-has-to-carry/), if you are moving between the two architectures

- [Which columns can be added, and which cannot](https://1494labs.com/notes/which-columns-can-be-added/), once both books are one table

- [What one ledger looks like in practice](https://1494labs.com/fund-accounting-software/)

- [Securities and positions](https://docs.1494labs.com/guide/securities-and-positions/) in the product docs: lots, prices and corporate actions

## How we think about this

1494 Labs is built on the second model: the accounting book of record and the
investment book of record are views over one ledger, and the arithmetic is
re-checked every morning.

[Request a demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact)

# Converting from a fund administrator: prove the first close

Agree the handoff date, reconcile the opening records and reproduce the next fee calculation before accepting the new book.

Fund operations · November 3, 2026

## Agree what is changing hands

Start by naming the accounting record your team will maintain and the services the administrator will continue to provide. Set a cutover date with an approved NAV, ledger and investor statements. Assign an owner to each open reconciliation item and each source file. A data export is an input to the handoff; acceptance requires evidence that the new book works.

1. **Collect one consistent opening pack.** Take the trial balance, investment positions, cash reconciliations, investor capital and fee schedules at the same approved date. Preserve the original exports.

2. **Map the records.** Match ledger accounts, investment identifiers, investor accounts and currencies. Resolve duplicate or missing identifiers before loading balances.

3. **Carry the calculation state.** Include high-water marks, loss carryforwards, equalization balances, side-pocket participation and unused fee credits where applicable. For private equity, preserve dated cash flows needed by the agreed waterfall and performance calculations.

4. **Reconcile the opening book.** Match the ledger to NAV, positions to investment controls and every investor balance to the approved statements. Record each difference separately and keep unrelated breaks visible.

5. **Run a parallel period.** Use the same dated transactions, valuations and agreement terms. Compare fees and allocations before comparing final statements.

6. **Accept the evidence.** Have the controller approve the opening reconciliation, the parallel-period results and the process for correcting any remaining items.

## A fee-state acceptance test

Assume an investor opens with 5,000 shares at $80 and a high-water mark of $100 per share. Its opening value is $400,000 and its remaining loss below the mark is $100,000. A conversion can load the $400,000 balance correctly while losing that fee state.

As a test, recover the gross value to $100 per share with no intervening capital activity. Under an agreed high-water-mark-only fee, the recovery should generate no incentive fee. A fee charged on the $100,000 recovery signals that the imported balance and imported fee state need separate investigation.

## Keep the transition reviewable

Save the source pack, mapping, rejected records, approved adjustments and signed reconciliation together. Confirm who can correct the new book, how closed history remains available and how the team will handle a late administrator adjustment.

1494 Labs supports imports, configured fees and a traceable ledger. Bring a representative opening pack and the next-period acceptance tests to a [demo](https://1494labs.com/#contact), and agree the conversion scope before setting a live date.

Related: [what an opening balance has to carry](https://1494labs.com/notes/what-an-opening-balance-has-to-carry/) and [bringing data in](https://docs.1494labs.com/guide/bringing-data-in/).
